findings.finding: The test obligation's subprocess partition is self-inconsistent on its face. The first sentence places render() in 'a dedicated isolated child Node process' and then continues, in the same uninterrupted procedure, with 'Verify the normal Existing value, then clear require.cache ... assert Screen.Existing === S ... Restore both cache entries in finally', which reads as the same process. A later sentence then states 'Run the sentinel block once in an isolated child Node process, independently of render and toggle assertions', which requires a different process from render. The two readings conflict: under the first, the sentinel block shares a process with render and so violates the explicit 'independently of render' requirement. The closing constraint 'Neither block may share module registry or selection state with another block' further uses a two-block formulation for what the text describes as three blocks (render, sentinel, toggle). Nothing in the gate disambiguates this — runDeliveredTests only executes `node tests/ui.test.js` and checks exit status, source hashes and write scope — so either partition passes, and an implementer may deliver a test that contradicts one sentence of its own obligation. The identical wording is reproduced verbatim in PROOF-34d4915acefae7f6303de490.expected and in the change intent of CHG-eece072cdc945f6a2a1729fb.

findings.finding: The plan grants the implementer explicit freedom over how the frame box is sized ("CSS declarations may be inline or in a stylesheet"; "CSS placement ... not certified. No inline-style ... shape is required"), but the orchestration-owned negative control can only perturb a subset of those mechanisms. negativeRenderFault strips the frame tag's style attribute and injects style="width:403px!important;height:874px!important;box-sizing:border-box!important;border:0!important;padding:0!important". It does not neutralise min-width/max-width clamping, flex/grid main-size resolution, or inline-size. A plan-permitted stylesheet such as [data-figma-id="4478:7209"]{min-width:402px;max-width:402px} or {flex:0 0 402px} keeps the used width at 402px despite the injected width:403px!important, because max/min-width clamp the used width after cascade and flex-basis takes precedence over width for a flex item. In that case the injected fault produces no measurement change, compare() does not throw, rejection stays undefined, and the driver aborts the whole qualification at VNEXT_FIGMA_REAL_NEGATIVE_NOT_REFUSED even though the delivery is correct and passed both viewports. A second, independent instance of the same mismatch: the injector locates the frame with /\bdata-figma-id\s*=\s*(["'])(.*?)\1/g, which requires a quoted attribute value, whereas the observer resolves the same element with querySelectorAll('[data-figma-id]'); a valid unquoted attribute (data-figma-id=4478:7209) passes measurement but makes the injector throw VNEXT_FIGMA_REAL_FAULT_TARGET_MISSING. Both failures are fail-closed rather than false-approving, but they turn a conforming implementation into a failed run, and the implementer has no way to know which CSS mechanism is actually required because the plan declares CSS placement uncertified.

findings.required_correction: Reconcile the permitted implementation freedom with the negative control. Either (a) state in the implementation_constraints of the geometry plan item that the frame's used width and height must be overridable by an inline !important width/height declaration — i.e. forbid min/max-size clamping, flex/grid main-size resolution and inline-size on the measured frame, and require a quoted data-figma-id attribute value — or (b) declare as an orchestration dependency that the fault injector must additionally force min-width/max-width/min-height/max-height:none and flex:none (and match unquoted attribute values) so that every CSS mechanism the plan permits is perturbable. Do not leave the negative control's effectiveness dependent on an implementation choice the plan declares uncertified.

findings.finding: The FUNCTIONAL_TEST proof of record for the two documentary scenarios names tests/ui.test.js as its target (target_test_impact_id IMP-185feab7132f38301a3089f0) and states that the Node test's 'receipt records the target path, exact source hashes and exit status'. However nothing from that Node execution reaches the evidence set the independent implementation reviewer actually validates. The only hash-bound artifact behind every measurement and scenario row is execution.json (artifact_path:'execution.json'), whose scenarios object is populated exclusively from the browser observation; the Node receipt is written to <output>/functional-test-initial.json, a sibling of the reviewed directory <output>/initial-review, and the reviewer is granted only --add-dir <evidenceDirectory>. Consequently the dossier's observed_files contains execution.json alone: neither the Node test's exit status nor its source hashes are present or readable at review time. The net effect is that the scenario proof the plan labels FUNCTIONAL_TEST is attested solely by toggle() calls made in the same browser JavaScript realm as the implementation — the realm the plan's own residual risk identifies as not isolated from tampering — while the genuinely realm-isolated Node subprocesses contribute evidence that is invisible to the reviewer. The gate is real and fail-closed, so this is not a false-approval path, but the proof obligation as planned cannot be independently verified from the evidence it ships.

findings.finding: The visual proof obligations state that geometry must be measured at BOTH 402x874 and the independent 503x971 viewport, that 'Equality at the required viewport alone is insufficient', and that rendered.png, rendered.html and browser-facts.json must be retained at each viewport. The driver does implement this and fails closed on divergence. However the second viewport leaves no trace in the verifiable evidence set: measurement rows are emitted only for d.rule.viewports, which is [402], and verifyMeasurements binds rows only to viewports listed in the frozen rule, so the 503x971 observation produces no measurement, no assertion coverage and no hash-bound artifact. The independent-viewport browser-facts.json, the provenance hashes (screen_source_sha256, preserved_source_sha256, loaded_document_sha256, canonical/measured mount hashes) and both screenshots are all written to disk but never hashed into the dossier. The falsification condition is therefore guaranteed only by one orchestration script's control flow, not by reviewable evidence. Note that the assertions themselves cannot carry a second viewport: validateCoverage requires a.expected and a.figma_reference.observable to be byte-identical to the frozen Figma rule, so the fix belongs in the proof evidence, not in the assertion or the Figma source viewports.
